orig_text:
|  Note: An endpoint that learns of stream closure after sending
      |  all data can close a stream by sending a STREAM frame with a
      |  zero-length Data field and the END_STREAM flag set.  This is
      |  only possible if the endpoint does not send trailers, as the
      |  END_STREAM flag appears on a HEADERS frame in that case; see
      |  Section 8.1.
correct_text:
|  Note: An endpoint that learns of stream closure after sending
      |  all data can close a stream by sending a DATA frame with a
      |  zero-length Data field and the END_STREAM flag set.  This is
      |  only possible if the endpoint does not send trailers, as the
      |  END_STREAM flag appears on a HEADERS frame in that case; see
      |  Section 8.1.
notes: Since STREAM frame is not defined in HTTP/2, I assume this is a DATA frame. This is probably a typo, possibly confused with the QUIC specification.

orig_text:
-  an OPTIONS request for an "http" or "https" URI that does not
   include a path component; these MUST include a ":path" pseudo-
   header field with a value of '*' (see Section 7.1 of [HTTP]).
correct_text:
-  an OPTIONS request for an "http" or "https" URI that does not
   include a path or query component; these MUST include a
   ":path" pseudo-header field with a value of '*' (see
   Section 7.1 of [HTTP]).
notes:
The :path definition includes both the path and query components, but the
OPTIONS exception tests only for an absent path. RFC 9112 Section 3.2.4
limits the corresponding conversion to "*" to an empty path and no query
component.

For example, a valid HTTP/1.1 OPTIONS request to a proxy with absolute-form
request-target https://example.com?x=1 has an empty path and a query. Its
HTTP/2 :path is /?x=1, not *. A present but empty query likewise needs its
delimiter preserved: https://example.com? maps to /?.

Reading the exception as limited to server-wide OPTIONS gives the intended
result, but that limitation is missing from its stated condition. This is
an instruction conflict, not a claim that the combined HTTP rules permit
query loss or that deployed implementations lose queries.

Adding "or query" makes the condition explicit while preserving server-wide
OPTIONS, ordinary path/query construction, and the other request mappings.

RFC 9114 Section 4.3.1 contains the corresponding path-only OPTIONS condition.
